root_cause: Hermit's `HermitItemCountService::get_item_counts` builds its `ItemCounts` via the shared helper `counts_from_type_map`, which sets `item_count: by_type.values().sum()` — the grand total of all matched rows (500 in the 500-movie fixture). Result: Jellyfin returns ItemCount=0, Hermit returns ItemCount=500 for the same library — the sole mismatched field (all per-type counts match because the fixture is all Movies, so only the Movie bucket is nonzero on both sides). faithfulness: Real Jellyfin's Jellyfin.Api LibraryController.GetItemCounts returns an ItemCounts (LibrarySummary) with only Album/Episode/Movie/Series/Song/MusicVideo/BoxSet/Book counts assigned via GetCount per BaseItemKind; ItemCount, ArtistCount, ProgramCount, and TrailerCount are never set and default to 0. root_cause:
Four independent divergences: three are real Hermit bugs rooted in hand-transcribed/hardcoded localization data plus an incorrectly-unconditional content-type block; the fourth (ExternalIdInfos) is a faithful-empty gap.

1) Countries (missing many): Hermit's countries come from a hardcoded 10-row table COUNTRY_ROWS at crates/hermit-core/src/localization_manager.rs:48-59 (US/GB/CA/AU/DE/FR/ES/IT/JP/NL only). Jellyfin loads its bundled Emby.Server.Implementations/Localization/countries.json — 197 ISO-3166 entries incl. Name="029" (Caribbean) and TwoLetterISORegionName="AT" (Austria). get_countries() (line 167) maps only the 10 rows, so ~187 countries are absent.

2) ParentalRatingOptions[NC-17].RatingScore.score and .Value mismatch: Hermit's US_RATINGS table (localization_manager.rs:63-75) hand-transcribes NC-17 as score 18, no subScore. Jellyfin's Ratings/us.json groups NC-17 with TV-MA at score=17, subScore=1. So Hermit reports score 18 (should be 17), omits subScore=1, and the derived Value differs. US_RATINGS is a lossy hand-port overall: also omits Approved, TV-Y7(7), the -D/-L/-S/-V subScore variants, TV-X/TV-AO(18), and drops all subScores.

3) ContentTypeOptions (Hermit-only extra): item_content_type_options() at crates/hermit-api/src/handlers/item_update.rs:45-58 always returns the full 7-option list and get_metadata_editor (line 563) always assigns it. Jellyfin's ItemUpdateController.GetMetadataEditorInfo only sets ContentTypeOptions inside a guard: item is a plain library item AND (inheritedContentType is null OR configuredContentType is not null). For a plain library Movie inheritedContentType="movies" (non-null) and configuredContentType=null, so the guard is false and ContentTypeOptions stays its default empty array. Hermit emits 7 options where Jellyfin emits [].

4) ExternalIdInfos[] mismatch: the running server wires LocalProviderManager::new(Vec::new()) (apps/hermit-server/src/state.rs:276); get_external_id_infos (crates/hermit-providers/src/provider_manager.rs:853-858) returns that empty vec for every item. Jellyfin returns per-item-type IExternalId descriptors (TheMovieDb, Imdb, Tvdb, TheMovieDbCollection, Zap2It...). Hermit has no populated external-ID registry (remote providers feature-gated off per CLAUDE.md) — faithful-empty/deferred gap, not an extension artifact.
proposed_fix:
Three real fixes (ExternalIdInfos is a separate deferred item):

FIX A — Countries: Replace hardcoded COUNTRY_ROWS with Jellyfin's bundled countries.json. Vendor Emby.Server.Implementations/Localization/countries.json into hermit-core (e.g. crates/hermit-core/src/data/countries.json), embed via include_str!, parse in get_countries() into CountryInfo{name, display_name, two_letter_iso_region_name, three_letter_iso_region_name}. Yields all 197 entries (029, AT, ...). Faithful port = copy file verbatim.

FIX B — Parental ratings: Replace hand-written US_RATINGS with Jellyfin's bundled Ratings/us.json (countryCode/supportsSubScores/ratings[] with ratingStrings[] and ratingScore{score,subScore}). Embed the file, expand each ratingStrings entry into a ParentalRating carrying the group's score AND subScore. Fixes NC-17 to score=17/subScore=1 and adds missing strings/subScores. Ideally embed the whole Ratings/ directory keyed by metadata_country_code, matching Jellyfin's loader.

FIX C — ContentTypeOptions guard: In get_metadata_editor (item_update.rs:557-564) stop unconditionally setting content_type_options. Port the C# guard: only populate when the item is a plain library item and (inheritedContentType.is_none() || configuredContentType.is_some()); when inheritedContentType is None or == tvshows, filter to Inherit + Shows only. Since the handler currently can't compute inherited/configured content type (it hardcodes content_type: None and the collection-folder tree is unported), the minimal correct interim fix is to default content_type_options to Vec::new() for plain library items — matching Jellyfin's empty array for the common non-folder Movie case.
faithfulness: Jellyfin loads countries from bundled countries.json (197 ISO-3166 entries incl. 029/AT), parental ratings from per-country Ratings/*.json (us.json: NC-17 grouped with TV-MA at score=17 subScore=1, plus subScore variants and TV-X/TV-AO=18), and only sets MetadataEditorInfo.ContentTypeOptions under the folder/collection-type guard in GetMetadataEditorInfo (empty array for a plain library Movie). ExternalIdInfos is per-item-type from registered IExternalId providers; Hermit legitimately has none wired (remote providers feature-gated off), so [] there is a deferred-subsystem gap rather than a bug in this handler.
collision_risk: Low-to-medium. Embedding countries.json/us.json touches only localization_manager.rs data + get_countries/get_parental_ratings; existing rstest oracles keyed to old US_RATINGS scores (e.g. NC-17=18) must be updated to the correct Jellyfin values — expected, the JSON is the oracle. The ContentTypeOptions guard change is localized to get_metadata_editor and its handler test (any batch asserting 7 options flips to expect []). No cross-crate signature changes.
verify: After fixes: (1) cargo nextest run -p hermit-core and -p hermit-api. (2) Boot the server and curl an authed GET /Items/{movieId}/MetadataEditor: assert Countries contains {Name:"029"} and a {TwoLetterISORegionName:"AT"} entry (jq '.Countries|length' ~= 197); ParentalRatingOptions NC-17 has RatingScore.score==17 and RatingScore.subScore==1; ContentTypeOptions == [] for a plain movie. (3) Re-run the differential parity harness for this op — the countries-missing, NC-17 mismatch, and ContentTypeOptions-extra diffs should be gone (ExternalIdInfos[] remains a documented deferred gap).

root_cause:
The response is assembled by a hand-written, guessed provider registry and per-type image tables in crates/hermit-providers/src/library_options.rs, not by projecting the real provider set. Three concrete divergences, one accepted:

1) MISSING (real bug) — TypeOptions[2].ImageFetchers & TypeOptions[3].ImageFetchers (Episode, Movie) lack "Embedded Image Extractor" and "Screen Grabber". These are Jellyfin's two built-in ffmpeg-backed image providers (EmbeddedImageProvider + VideoImageProvider in MediaBrowser.Providers/MediaInfo). They are NOT plugins/extensions — stock Jellyfin always ships them for video types. Hermit's registry in library_options.rs::providers() simply omits them, even though the backing capability exists (hermit-mediaencoding media_encoder.rs::extract_video_image / extract_image_arguments with thumbnail sampling — the exact ffmpeg screen-grab + embedded-image extraction those two providers use). So this is an unregistered-provider gap, not a faithful-empty.

2) MISMATCH (real bug) — TypeOptions[*].SupportedImageTypes[1..3] and array length. In Jellyfin SupportedImageTypes is _providerManager.GetSupportedImageTypes(type): the union of ImageTypes the registered image providers actually supply for that type, in provider-registration order. Hermit hardcodes a fixed 11-element list (supported_image_types()) independent of providers, so both the set and its ordering (index 1 = Art, etc.) diverge — compounded by the two missing providers that would contribute Primary/Backdrop/Thumb.

3) MISMATCH (real bug) — TypeOptions[*].DefaultImageOptions[*].Type/Limit/MinWidth and array length. Jellyfin sources these from the per-type static table in MediaBrowser.Model.Configuration.TypeOptions (DefaultImageOptions), which Hermit has NOT ported — hermit-model/src/configuration.rs has a TypeOptions DTO but no default-image-options table; library_options.rs::default_image_options() substitutes a guessed Primary/Backdrop(1280)/Logo set whose per-index Type/Limit/MinWidth and length don't match Jellyfin.

4) EXTRA (accepted expected-extension) — MediaSegmentProviders[IntroSkipper], SubtitleFetchers[Open Subtitles], TypeOptions[0].ImageFetchers[The Open Movie Database] are Hermit's by-design compiled-in extensions; correct to keep.
proposed_fix:
In crates/hermit-providers/src/library_options.rs:

(a) Register the two built-in image providers in providers() (library_options.rs:77-131):
   - name "Embedded Image Extractor", caps &[Cap::ImageFetcher], types &["Movie","Episode","Series","Season","MusicVideo","Video"] (Jellyfin's video-ish types), default_enabled true, compiled true.
   - name "Screen Grabber", caps &[Cap::ImageFetcher], types &["Movie","Episode","MusicVideo","Video"], default_enabled true, compiled true.
   Both are backed by hermit-mediaencoding (extract_video_image), so compiled:true is honest, not a stub. This clears the four "missing" ImageFetchers.

(b) Derive SupportedImageTypes from the registered image providers instead of the fixed list. Replace the hardcoded supported_image_types() output in library_options_info() (line 219) with the union of ImageTypes contributed by each compiled provider that applies to the type, preserving provider-registration order — mirroring _providerManager.GetSupportedImageTypes. This requires giving each Provider the ImageType set it supplies (e.g. Nfo/LocalImages -> the full local set; Embedded Image Extractor -> Primary; Screen Grabber -> Primary; TMDB/OMDb -> Primary/Backdrop/Logo/Thumb per Jellyfin). Match Jellyfin's per-provider supported-type declarations verbatim.

(c) Port Jellyfin's per-type DefaultImageOptions from MediaBrowser.Model.Configuration.TypeOptions into a faithful table (ideally in hermit-model/src/configuration.rs next to the TypeOptions DTO, then consumed by default_image_options()), replacing the guessed Primary/Backdrop(1280)/Logo set. Transliterate the C# static table's Type/Limit/MinWidth and ordering exactly per item type (Series, Season, Episode, Movie, etc.).

Leave the three "extra" IntroSkipper/OpenSubtitles/OMDb entries as-is (expected-extension).
faithfulness: Stock Jellyfin, for a TV/movie library, returns per video type (Movie/Episode) ImageFetchers that include the built-in "Embedded Image Extractor" (EmbeddedImageProvider) and "Screen Grabber" (VideoImageProvider) alongside remote fetchers; SupportedImageTypes = the provider-derived union (GetSupportedImageTypes); and DefaultImageOptions = the per-type static table in MediaBrowser.Model.Configuration.TypeOptions. Hermit currently omits the two built-in image providers and hardcodes guessed SupportedImageTypes/DefaultImageOptions tables. Note the harness's Jellyfin instance also has NO extensions, so the OMDb/IntroSkipper/OpenSubtitles entries showing as "extra" is expected (Hermit-by-design), not a Jellyfin behavior to match.
collision_risk: Touches the same file/tables another parity fix for GET /Libraries/MetadataOptions or ProviderManager::get_all_metadata_plugins would edit (all_metadata_plugins() and supported_image_types() live in the same module and share the registry). Coordinate: the SupportedImageTypes derivation change also affects all_metadata_plugins()'s supported_image_types field. The two existing unit tests in library_options.rs (movie_options_expose_real_fetchers_and_savers, etc.) will need updating for the new providers/tables.
verify: After the fix, curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:8096/Libraries/AvailableOptions?libraryContentType=tvshows' with an admin token and jq the TypeOptions for Episode/Movie: assert ImageFetchers contains both "Embedded Image Extractor" and "Screen Grabber"; then re-run the differential sweep (benchmark/parity.sh single op GET /Libraries/AvailableOptions) and confirm the four "missing" ImageFetchers and the SupportedImageTypes/DefaultImageOptions mismatches clear, with only the three by-design "extra" extension entries remaining. Update/extend the rstest cases in library_options.rs to lock the new Jellyfin-matching Type/Limit/MinWidth values.

root_cause: The handler `get_guide_info` in crates/hermit-api/src/handlers/live_tv.rs:52-54 is a hardcoded stub that returns `GuideInfo::default()`. `GuideInfo` derives `Default`, so both `StartDate` and `EndDate` serialize to chrono's `DateTime<Utc>::default()` = the Unix epoch `"1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"`. It never consults the Live TV manager or the clock. Jellyfin's `LiveTvController.GetGuideInfo` -> `LiveTvManager.GetGuideInfo()` computes `StartDate = DateTime.UtcNow` and `EndDate = UtcNow.AddDays(GetGuideDays())`, where `GetGuideDays()` clamps the configured `LiveTvOptions.GuideDays` to 1..=14 and defaults to 7 when null/out-of-range. So Jellyfin returns a real now-relative window (Start < End, both current) while Hermit returns epoch-zero on both fields -> the harness flags both StartDate and EndDate as mismatches. This is not date-volatility noise: epoch-0 for both (with StartDate==EndDate) is a substantively wrong body, and the field is present, not empty, so it is not faithful-empty.
faithfulness: Jellyfin always returns a real now-relative window for GuideInfo regardless of whether any tuners/channels exist: StartDate = UtcNow, EndDate = UtcNow + GuideDays (default 7, clamped 1..14). It does not depend on library state, so an empty fixture still yields non-epoch dates.
collision_risk: Low. Isolated one-handler change; DTO already exists and round-trips. Post-fix the StartDate/EndDate values become now-relative and the harness's date-denylist/normalization will collapse them to match Jellyfin's, clearing the mismatch. If a trait method is added instead, it touches LiveTvManager (trait + HermitLiveTvManager impl) — object-safe and additive, no signature changes to existing methods.
verify: Run Hermit and Jellyfin against the empty fixture: `curl -s .../LiveTv/GuideInfo` on both. Before fix Hermit returns `{"StartDate":"1970-01-01T00:00:00Z","EndDate":"1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"}`; after fix it returns StartDate≈now and EndDate≈now+7d (Start<End), matching Jellyfin's shape. Re-run the differential harness for GET /LiveTv/GuideInfo and confirm mismatch=[] (dates normalized/denylisted).

root_cause: Hermit's HermitLiveTvManager::get_live_tv_info (crates/hermit-livetv/src/manager.rs:169-187) gates the entire Services list AND IsEnabled on the existence of configured tuner hosts: `enabled = !tuners.is_empty()`, services empty when no tuners, and the only service it would ever emit is one named "M3U/XMLTV". On the fixture no tuner hosts are configured, so Hermit returns {Services:[], IsEnabled:false, EnabledUsers:[]}. Jellyfin's LiveTvManager.GetLiveTvInfo builds Services from the DI-registered ILiveTvService collection, which ALWAYS contains the built-in DefaultLiveTvService/EmbyTV (whose `Name => "Emby"`), registered unconditionally regardless of tuner config. Jellyfin then sets IsEnabled = Services.Count > 0, which is therefore always true. Hence Jellyfin returns Services=[{Name="Emby",...}] and IsEnabled=true even with zero tuners. Both flagged diffs (missing Emby service, IsEnabled mismatch) stem from this one modeling difference: Hermit ties service presence to tuner config; Jellyfin always ships the built-in Emby service.
proposed_fix: In get_live_tv_info (manager.rs:169-187), always emit the built-in Emby service and set is_enabled unconditionally, mirroring Jellyfin's DefaultLiveTvService. Concretely: build services starting with LiveTvServiceInfo{ name: Some("Emby".to_owned()), status: LiveTvServiceStatus::Ok, is_visible: true, ..default() } (this is the DefaultLiveTvService), optionally appending the M3U/XMLTV entry when tuner hosts exist; then is_enabled = !services.is_empty() (i.e. always true). Also populate enabled_users from the users whose policy enables Live TV (Jellyfin fills EnabledUsers with User.Id "N"-format for users where IsLiveTvEnabled) instead of the hardcoded empty Vec — that array is currently always empty on Hermit and will diverge whenever a user has Live TV access. Minimal correctness for the two flagged diffs only needs the always-present "Emby" service + is_enabled=true.
faithfulness: Real Jellyfin always registers DefaultLiveTvService (EmbyTV) in DI; GetServiceInfos() therefore always yields at least one service named "Emby", and IsEnabled = Services.Count > 0 is always true, independent of tuner-host configuration. EnabledUsers lists every user with Live TV enabled in their policy. Hermit only emits a service (named "M3U/XMLTV", never "Emby") when a tuner host row exists, so it reports IsEnabled=false and an empty Services on an unconfigured instance — a faithful port must always include the Emby service.
collision_risk: Low. Changes are confined to get_live_tv_info; the LiveTvServiceInfo/LiveTvInfo DTOs already match the spec and need no change. One existing unit test (manager.rs:853) asserts is_enabled true only after adding a tuner — after the fix is_enabled is always true, so that test still passes; any test asserting is_enabled==false on an empty instance (none found) would need updating. EnabledUsers population touches the user manager, slightly wider but optional for the two flagged diffs.
verify: With a fresh Hermit (no tuner hosts): curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8096/LiveTv/Info (authed) and assert Services[0].Name=="Emby" and IsEnabled==true. Unit: extend the manager test to assert get_live_tv_info().services contains a service named "Emby" and is_enabled is true BEFORE any tuner host is saved.

root_cause:
Jellyfin's GetDefaultListingProvider returns `new ListingsProviderInfo()`, and the C# ListingsProviderInfo constructor seeds the four category arrays and sets EnableAllTuners=true:
  NewsCategories = ["news","journalism","documentary","current affairs"]
  SportsCategories = ["sports","basketball","baseball","football"]
  KidsCategories = ["kids","family","children","childrens","disney"]
  MovieCategories = ["movie"]
  EnableAllTuners = true
Hermit's handler also returns `ListingsProviderInfo::default()`, but the struct uses `#[derive(Default)]` (crates/hermit-model/src/live_tv.rs:622). The derived default leaves the four `Option<Vec<String>>` category fields as None (so `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"` omits them from JSON -> the four "missing" keys) and sets the `enable_all_tuners: bool` to false (Rust bool default) instead of true -> the EnableAllTuners "mismatch". Not a localization/data-table issue; a hand-rolled Default was needed to mirror the C# ctor and was never written.
faithfulness: Jellyfin returns a ListingsProviderInfo built by its default constructor, which pre-populates NewsCategories/SportsCategories/KidsCategories/MovieCategories with the fixed English seed keyword lists above and sets EnableAllTuners=true (EnabledTuners and ChannelMappings empty). GetDefaultListingProvider passes no config, so these ctor defaults are exactly what a stock Jellyfin emits.
collision_risk: Low. ListingsProviderInfo::default() is also used as the `..Default::default()` base when POSTing/persisting providers; giving it the seed categories matches Jellyfin (which stores those same ctor defaults when a provider is added without categories), so it improves parity there too rather than regressing. Only touches one DTO in hermit-model; no schema/route change, contract-superset test unaffected.
verify: After the change, GET /LiveTv/ListingProviders/Default should serialize with EnableAllTuners:true plus the four category arrays. Quick unit assertion: `let d = ListingsProviderInfo::default(); assert!(d.enable_all_tuners); assert_eq!(d.movie_categories.as_deref(), Some(&["movie".to_string()][..]));` and `serde_json::to_value(&d)` contains keys NewsCategories/SportsCategories/KidsCategories/MovieCategories. Re-run the differential harness for GET /LiveTv/ListingProviders/Default -> expect empty missing/extra/mismatch.

root_cause:
The Hermit handler `get_default_timer` (crates/hermit-api/src/handlers/live_tv.rs:457-459) returns a bare `Json(SeriesTimerInfoDto::default())` — every field is Rust's zero/false/None/empty. It never ports Jellyfin's `GetNewTimerDefaults` logic (it doesn't even call the LiveTvManager). Jellyfin builds this DTO through DefaultLiveTvService.GetNewTimerDefaultsAsync + LiveTvManager.GetNewTimerDefaults + LiveTvDtoService.GetSeriesTimerInfoDto, which sets meaningful, non-default values. Field-by-field vs Jellyfin v10.11.8:
- Type: SeriesTimerInfoDto ctor sets `Type = "SeriesTimer"` (MediaBrowser.Model/LiveTv/SeriesTimerInfoDto.cs:27). Hermit `type_ = None` and is skip_serializing_if none → MISSING.
- ServiceName: LiveTvDtoService.cs:139 sets `ServiceName = service.Name` = "Emby" (DefaultLiveTvService.ServiceName). Hermit None → MISSING.
- DayPattern: LiveTvDtoService.cs:154 = GetDayPattern(7 days) = Daily. Hermit None → MISSING.
- Days: DefaultLiveTvService.cs:417-431 sets all 7 (Sunday..Saturday). Hermit `[]` → MISMATCH.
- RecordAnyTime: true (DefaultLiveTvService.cs:414). Hermit false → MISMATCH.
- RecordNewOnly: true (line 415). Hermit false → MISMATCH.
- SkipEpisodesInLibrary: = RecordNewOnly = true (line 437). Hermit false → MISMATCH.
- StartDate/EndDate: never set on the SeriesTimerInfo, so C# DateTime.MinValue → "0001-01-01T00:00:00.0000000Z". Hermit DateTime<Utc>::default() = Unix epoch "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z" → MISMATCH (both non-volatile constants, so the harness legitimately flags them).
- ChannelId: Jellyfin leaves the empty GUID (info.ChannelId empty → dto.ChannelId stays Guid.Empty). Hermit Uuid::default() is also all-zeros; the flag is a serialization/normalization artifact of the epoch/other-field diffs on the same object rather than a distinct semantic gap — it resolves once the DTO is populated like Jellyfin's.
This is not a deferred/faithful-empty case: Live TV IS wired in Hermit (hermit-livetv is active, GET returns 200), so the endpoint is live but returns wrong data that jellyfin-web reads to prefill the New Recording / Record Series dialog (all-days, record-new-only, paddings).
proposed_fix:
Port Jellyfin's GetNewTimerDefaults instead of returning ::default(). Best: add a `get_default_timer()` method on the LiveTvManager trait (hermit-traits) implemented in hermit-livetv, and have the handler call it (falling back to the populated DTO even when no listing provider is configured, since Jellyfin's DefaultLiveTvService always answers). Populate the DTO exactly like Jellyfin:
  base.type_ = Some("SeriesTimer"),
  base.service_name = Some("Emby"),   // DefaultLiveTvService.ServiceName; Hermit reuses this string elsewhere
  base.channel_id = Uuid::nil(),      // empty
  base.start_date / base.end_date = DateTime::<Utc>::MIN_UTC (0001-01-01T00:00:00Z) to match C# DateTime.MinValue, NOT the Unix-epoch Default,
  base.pre_padding_seconds = max(config.PrePaddingSeconds, 0),
  base.post_padding_seconds = max(config.PostPaddingSeconds, 0),  // pull from LiveTvOptions in server config
  base.keep_until = KeepUntil::UntilDeleted,
  record_any_time = true, record_new_only = true, skip_episodes_in_library = true, record_any_channel = false,
  days = vec![Sunday,Monday,Tuesday,Wednesday,Thursday,Friday,Saturday],
  day_pattern = Some(DayPattern::Daily),   // GetDayPattern(7)==Daily
  image_tags = empty map.
Keep the DateTime constant question in mind: C# DateTime.MinValue is 0001-01-01; Rust chrono has DateTime::<Utc>::MIN_UTC — use that rather than a magic literal. Also transliterate GetDayPattern (7→Daily, 5 weekdays→Weekdays, Sat+Sun→Weekends) as a reusable helper since UpdateSeriesTimer will need it too. No new magic numbers to surface (paddings come from config; the 7/5/2 day counts are Jellyfin's oracle values, not tunable).
faithfulness: Jellyfin ALWAYS answers this endpoint via the built-in DefaultLiveTvService (service name \"Emby\") regardless of whether any tuner/listing provider is configured. It returns a SeriesTimerInfoDto with Type=\"SeriesTimer\", ServiceName=\"Emby\", all 7 Days, DayPattern=Daily, RecordAnyTime=RecordNewOnly=SkipEpisodesInLibrary=true, RecordAnyChannel=false, KeepUntil=UntilDeleted, paddings from LiveTvOptions (default 0), and DateTime.MinValue Start/End dates. jellyfin-web consumes these to seed the record-series dialog.
collision_risk: Low. Touches only the get_default_timer handler plus a new trait method/impl and a GetDayPattern helper in hermit-livetv/hermit-model. No route/schema change (SeriesTimerInfoDto already has all fields), so contract_superset stays green. The DateTime::MIN_UTC change is localized to this default builder. Overlaps only with any concurrent Live TV timer-CRUD work (UpdateSeriesTimer would want the same GetDayPattern helper — coordinate to share it).
verify: Unit test in hermit-livetv (or hermit-model) asserting the produced DTO serializes to Type=\"SeriesTimer\", ServiceName=\"Emby\", Days length 7, DayPattern=\"Daily\", RecordAnyTime/RecordNewOnly/SkipEpisodesInLibrary all true, KeepUntil=\"UntilDeleted\", StartDate/EndDate == \"0001-01-01T00:00:00Z\". Then live check: curl -s -H 'Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=\"...\"' http://localhost:8096/LiveTv/Timers/Defaults | jq '{Type,ServiceName,DayPattern,Days,RecordAnyTime,RecordNewOnly,SkipEpisodesInLibrary}' and diff against the same call on real Jellyfin — the flagged missing/mismatch set should collapse to empty.

root_cause: Jellyfin's GetTunerHostTypes enumerates every registered ITunerHost implementation. Stock Jellyfin ships two built-in tuner hosts: M3UTunerHost (Id "m3u", Name "M3U Tuner") and HdHomerunHost (Id "hdhomerun", Name "HD Homerun"), so the endpoint returns two NameIdPair entries. Hermit's Live TV subsystem (crate hermit-livetv) implements only the M3U backend (only m3u.rs / xmltv.rs exist; no HDHomeRun network-tuner discovery/status/streaming code anywhere in the tree). Its handler therefore returns a single-element list [{"Name":"M3U Tuner","Id":"m3u"}]. The one type Jellyfin has that Hermit lacks is HDHomeRun. The harness's "Hermit returns empty" is imprecise — the handler is registered unconditionally and always returns the M3U pair; the real, substantive divergence is the missing hdhomerun entry, which is an un-ported backend rather than a fake/empty response.
proposed_fix: None needed. Hermit correctly advertises only the tuner-host type it actually implements (M3U). Adding "hdhomerun" to the list without a real HdHomerunHost backend (SSDP/HTTP device discovery, /discover.json + /lineup.json parsing, per-tuner status, and stream proxying) would violate the project rule "Never fake a deferred subsystem to make a route pass" — a client selecting that type would then fail on POST /LiveTv/TunerHosts. The correct closure of this gap is to port HdHomerunHost as a genuine second backend in hermit-livetv, at which point the handler should return both pairs. Until then, returning [M3U Tuner] is the faithful behavior. When ported, the exact Jellyfin values to emit are {Name:"HD Homerun", Id:"hdhomerun"}.
faithfulness: Jellyfin returns the Type/Name of each registered ITunerHost. Out of the box that is M3U ("m3u"/"M3U Tuner") and HDHomeRun ("hdhomerun"/"HD Homerun"). Hermit ships a working M3U tuner host and matches Jellyfin's M3U pair exactly; it has not ported the HDHomeRun network-tuner backend, so it omits that pair.
collision_risk: Low. The M3U handler is a fixed literal; nothing else depends on the returned list beyond clients populating the "add tuner" dropdown. Adding HDHomeRun later only appends an entry and requires the corresponding backend + POST /LiveTv/TunerHosts validation, contained within hermit-livetv.
verify: Run the server and: curl -s -H "Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=..." http://localhost:8096/LiveTv/TunerHosts/Types — expect [{"Name":"M3U Tuner","Id":"m3u"}] (non-empty, one entry). Compare to a stock Jellyfin instance which returns two entries including {"Name":"HD Homerun","Id":"hdhomerun"}. The single missing entry is the deferred HDHomeRun backend.

root_cause: Hermit's LocalizationManager.get_countries() returns a hardcoded 10-row stub (COUNTRY_ROWS at crates/hermit-core/src/localization_manager.rs:48-59: US, GB, CA, AU, DE, FR, ES, IT, JP, NL). Jellyfin's LocalizationManager.GetCountries() instead deserializes an embedded resource, Emby.Server.Implementations/Localization/countries.json, which lists ~139 ISO 3166 regions (Name, DisplayName, TwoLetterISORegionName, ThreeLetterISORegionName each). So the whole list differs: Hermit yields 10 CountryInfo objects, Jellyfin yields ~139. The self-describing comments ("compact embedded country dataset", "short CountryInfo list") confirm this was left as a deliberate stub. Note the sibling culture dataset (iso6392.txt, ~200 languages) IS fully vendored via include_str!, so only the countries table was left incomplete.
proposed_fix: Vendor Jellyfin 10.11.8's Emby.Server.Implementations/Localization/countries.json into crates/hermit-core/src/data/countries.json and load it the same way iso6392.txt is loaded. Concretely: (1) add `const COUNTRIES_JSON: &str = include_str!("data/countries.json");` next to the ISO6392 const (line ~44). (2) Deserialize it once in LocalizationManager::new (or lazily) into Vec<CountryInfo> (the JSON keys are PascalCase Name/DisplayName/TwoLetterISORegionName/ThreeLetterISORegionName, matching CountryInfo's serde). (3) Replace get_countries() (lines 167-177) to clone/return that vector instead of mapping COUNTRY_ROWS, and delete COUNTRY_ROWS. Preserve Jellyfin's ordering from the JSON file so the differential harness sees identical order. Existing tests (US present, "United Kingdom" present at lines 501-509) still pass since those countries remain in the full set. Note: CountryInfo fields are non-Option String in Hermit but nullable in the spec/JSON — a few Jellyfin rows have null ThreeLetterISORegionName; handle with #[serde(default)] on String or (more faithful) widen those fields to Option<String> to match the spec's nullable and emit null exactly as Jellyfin does. Recommend widening to Option<String> for exact parity.
faithfulness: Jellyfin returns the full contents of its embedded countries.json (~139 ISO 3166 regions) from GetCountries, unconditionally and unfiltered, in file order. It is bundled static data, not instance- or config-dependent, so faithful parity means shipping the identical dataset.
collision_risk: Low. Isolated to localization_manager.rs plus a new vendored data/countries.json asset. Only risk is the CountryInfo nullability decision (Option<String> vs String) which touches the DTO in hermit-model and could affect any other consumer of CountryInfo (metadata editor info) — but widening to Option is serde-compatible and matches the spec. No route/table changes; contract-superset test unaffected.
verify: After vendoring: `curl -s localhost:8096/Localization/Countries | jq length` should return ~139 (Jellyfin count) instead of 10, and `jq '.[] | select(.TwoLetterISORegionName=="BR")'` (or any country outside the stub 10, e.g. Brazil) should be present. Unit test: assert get_countries().len() matches the JSON entry count and contains a country not in the old stub (e.g. two_letter_iso_region_name == "BR"). Run the existing localization tests + differential harness on GET /Localization/Countries to confirm zero missing.

root_cause: Hermit synthesizes localization options from the WRONG data source. Jellyfin's LocalizationManager.GetLocalizationOptions() returns a fixed, curated list of UI-translation languages derived from its embedded translation catalog (Emby.Server.Implementations/Localization/Core/*.json) — roughly 35-40 entries, each with a NATIVE-language display Name (e.g. "Deutsch", "Français", "العربية", "简体中文") and a specific culture-code Value that is sometimes region-qualified (en-US, en-GB, fr-CA, pt-BR, zh-CN, zh-TW). Hermit instead builds the list at crates/hermit-core/src/localization_manager.rs:187-211 by iterating its ~200-language ISO 639 culture table (data/iso6392.txt), taking the English display_name truncated at the first ';'/',' as Name and the bare two-letter ISO 639-1 code as Value, skipping only empty/"en" entries and prepending a hardcoded {Name:"English", Value:"en-US"}. Result: Hermit emits ~190 entries with English names + bare two-letter codes; Jellyfin emits ~35 entries with native names + full culture codes. So every entry's Name and Value diverge, and the counts differ too — hence the "Name","Value" mismatch with empty missing/extra (the differ folds the whole array under those two keys). The code's own doc comment (lines 181-185) admits the catalog "is a hermit-server asset that this minimal port omits."
proposed_fix: Replace the synthesized list in get_localization_options() (localization_manager.rs:187-211) with Jellyfin's actual fixed LocalizationOption set. Port it verbatim from upstream jellyfin's LocalizationManager._localizationOptions / the Core translation catalog (each translation JSON file name is the culture Value; the native Name comes from Jellyfin's LocalizationOption(...) list). Best embodied as a static const table LOCALIZATION_OPTIONS: &[(&str /*Name*/, &str /*Value*/)] alongside the other embedded datasets (near US_RATINGS / COUNTRY_ROWS), then have get_localization_options() just map that table into Vec<LocalizationOption>. Do NOT derive it from the ISO 639 culture table. This is a data-completeness/wrong-source bug, not an instance or extension divergence.
faithfulness: Real Jellyfin returns a static curated array of ~35-40 LocalizationOption objects with native-language Names and specific (sometimes region-qualified) culture-code Values, sourced from the embedded UI-translation catalog — completely independent of the iso6392 culture list. It is the same fixed list on every instance (not config-dependent), so there is no instance-variance excuse.
collision_risk: Low. The only consumer is the get_localization_options handler; changing the table body doesn't touch signatures or other manager methods. Existing unit tests in batch13/batch16 use their own fake LocalizationManager impls, so they won't break; any test asserting the old synthesized contents in hermit-core would need updating to the new fixed list.
verify: After embedding Jellyfin's list, diff against a live Jellyfin: `curl -s localhost:8096/Localization/Options | jq 'sort_by(.Value)'` vs the same on Jellyfin — the two arrays should be element-for-element equal on Name and Value. Smallest unit check: assert get_localization_options() length ~35 (not ~190), contains {Name:"Deutsch",Value:"de"} and {Name:"English (United States)",Value:"en-US"}, and contains no bare-two-letter-only synthetic entries like {Name:"Zulu",Value:"zu"}.

root_cause:
Hermit's embedded US parental-rating dataset is a compact, hand-written stand-in that diverges from Jellyfin 10.11.8's bundled data on three axes, producing the observed missing/mismatch diff:

1) Data source mismatch. Jellyfin 10.11.8 loads per-country JSON files (Emby.Server.Implementations/Localization/Ratings/us.json), which carry supportsSubScores + score/subScore PAIRS and multiple ratingStrings per score. Hermit hardcodes only 11 (string,i32) tuples with NO subScore at all (crates/hermit-core/src/localization_manager.rs:63-75, US_RATINGS). That is why RatingScore.subScore is always absent from Hermit's response (\"missing subScore\").

2) Wrong scores -> RatingScore.score + Value mismatch. Value is derived (score?.Score) identically in both (confirmed vs MediaBrowser.Model/Entities/ParentalRating.cs), so the Value mismatch is purely a symptom of wrong score data. Concrete divergences from us.json: TV-MA should be score=17 subScore=1 (Hermit: 17, no subScore); NC-17 should be score=17 subScore=1 (Hermit: 18, no subScore); TV-Y7 should be 7 subScore=0; PG/TV-PG should be 10 subScore=0; R should be 17 subScore=0; TV-14 14 subScore=0; etc.

3) Missing rating strings / missing whole entries. Jellyfin flattens every ratingStrings token into its own ParentalRating (C# LocalizationManager.cs:82-90 builds dict per string; GetParentalRatings at :214 emits one entry per key). us.json yields ~60 rating strings (Approved, TV-Y7-FV, the full TV-PG-*/TV-14-*/TV-MA-* content-descriptor matrices, TV-X, TV-AO) that Hermit's 11-row table never produces -> \"(whole item)\" missing entries. Hermit also omits \"Approved\" from its base table (it only appears via the score==0 back-fill), whereas Jellyfin ships it explicitly in us.json.

The back-fill/ordering logic in get_parental_ratings (localization_manager.rs:261-321) faithfully mirrors C# GetParentalRatings (Unrated, Approved/10/13/14, 21, XXX=1000, Banned=1001, OrderBy Score ThenBy SubScore) — that part is correct. The bug is entirely the underlying US dataset being incomplete/wrong.
proposed_fix:
Replace the hand-written US_RATINGS table with Jellyfin's actual bundled data and load it faithfully:

Preferred (matches CLAUDE.md "port faithfully"): vendor Jellyfin 10.11.8's Ratings/*.json files as embedded assets (e.g. crates/hermit-core/src/data/ratings/us.json, gb.json, ...) and parse them in LocalizationManager::new the way C# LoadRatings does: for each ratingSystem, for each ratingEntry, for each ratingString, insert dict[ratingString] = ratingEntry.ratingScore (the SAME ParentalRatingScore for every string in that entry). This gives correct score+subScore and the full per-string flattening (one ParentalRating per string), fixing all three diff axes at once. Note countryCode in the file is lowercase ("us"); C# uses OrdinalIgnoreCase — Hermit already uppercases lookups (parental_ratings_for), so store keys uppercased or make the map case-insensitive.

Minimal (if only US parity is in scope for this pass): replace US_RATINGS: &[(&str,i32)] with the exact us.json entries as (&str, score, Option<i32> subScore), expanding every ratingStrings token to its own row:
  score 0 subScore 0: Approved, G, TV-G, TV-Y
  score 7 subScore 0: TV-Y7
  score 7 subScore 1: TV-Y7-FV
  score 10 subScore 0: PG, TV-PG
  score 10 subScore 1: TV-PG-D, TV-PG-L, TV-PG-S, TV-PG-V, TV-PG-DL, TV-PG-DS, TV-PG-DV, TV-PG-LS, TV-PG-LV, TV-PG-SV, TV-PG-DLS, TV-PG-DLV, TV-PG-DSV, TV-PG-LSV, TV-PG-DLSV
  score 13 subScore 0: PG-13
  score 14 subScore 0: TV-14
  score 14 subScore 1: TV-14-D ... TV-14-DLSV (same descriptor matrix)
  score 17 subScore 0: R
  score 17 subScore 1: NC-17, TV-MA, TV-MA-L, TV-MA-S, TV-MA-V, TV-MA-LS, TV-MA-LV, TV-MA-SV, TV-MA-LSV
  score 18 subScore 0: TV-X, TV-AO
Then in ::new build ParentalRatingScore::new(score, subScore) instead of ...new(score, None). No DTO changes needed — ParentalRatingScore already serializes subScore (entities_media.rs:198). Leave get_parental_ratings back-fill/sort untouched.

Also fix the stale doc comment at localization_manager.rs:62 ("Ratings/us.json ... common film/TV ratings") to reflect the full dataset.

Magic-number note for the user: the back-fill sentinels 1000 (XXX) and 1001 (Banned) and the 21 catch-all are Jellyfin-defined constants copied verbatim from C#, so they should stay hardcoded (they are contract values, not tunables).
faithfulness: Real Jellyfin 10.11.8 loads Emby.Server.Implementations/Localization/Ratings/us.json (supportsSubScores:true) into _allParentalRatings, one dict key per ratingString all sharing the entry's score/subScore, then GetParentalRatings() emits one ParentalRating per key (Value=score, RatingScore={score,subScore}), appends the Unrated/Approved/10/13/14/21/XXX/Banned back-fills when absent, and returns OrderBy(Score).ThenBy(SubScore). Its US response therefore contains ~60+ rating strings with subScores; Hermit currently returns 11 strings with no subScores and two wrong scores (NC-17=18, TV-MA=17/no-sub).
collision_risk: Low. Change is confined to the US_RATINGS constant + ::new construction in localization_manager.rs (and optionally new embedded data files). No trait/DTO signatures change. Callers get_rating_score / item_update.rs:558 / internal_items_query parental-rating filtering only benefit from the corrected/expanded table (more rating strings resolve, subScores now populated). Existing rstest cases in localization_manager.rs and entities_media.rs (parental_rating_score_* tests) should be checked — any test asserting the old 11-entry US list or NC-17=18 will need updating to the us.json oracle.
verify: After the fix, diff against the oracle: curl the running Hermit at GET /Localization/ParentalRatings and assert (a) an entry Name="TV-MA" with RatingScore={score:17,subScore:1} and Value=17; (b) Name="NC-17" score:17 subScore:1 (not 18); (c) Name="TV-Y7-FV" score:7 subScore:1 exists; (d) Name="Approved" present from data (score 0 subScore 0); (e) count of entries jumps from ~18 to ~65 and every content-descriptor string (e.g. TV-14-DLSV) is present. Compare the JSON array byte-for-byte (modulo denylisted volatile keys) to a real Jellyfin 10.11.8 /Localization/ParentalRatings response — they should match exactly. Add an rstest that loads us.json and asserts these tuples so the C# values stay the oracle.

root_cause:
The endpoint returns `state.config.configuration()` (handler `get_configuration`, crates/hermit-api/src/handlers/config.rs:64-69), which on a fresh install is the seeded document from `default_server_configuration()` in crates/hermit-core/src/configuration_manager.rs:83. Three of the seeded defaults do not match Jellyfin's `MediaBrowser.Model/Configuration/ServerConfiguration.cs` constructor defaults; the other two diffs are genuine per-instance runtime state.

REAL DEFAULT BUGS (config-defaults that should match Jellyfin):
1. PluginRepositories (missing "Jellyfin Stable"): Jellyfin's constructor seeds `PluginRepositories = [ RepositoryInfo { Name = "Jellyfin Stable", Url = "https://repo.jellyfin.org/files/plugin/manifest.json", Enabled = true } ]`. Hermit sets `plugin_repositories: Vec::new()` (configuration_manager.rs:134) so the whole item is absent. This is not an extension-provider case (those are IntroSkipper/OpenSubtitles/OMDb); the default upstream plugin repo is stock Jellyfin data that clients (the dashboard Catalog page) expect.
2. EnableLegacyAuthorization (false vs Jellyfin true): Jellyfin defaults `EnableLegacyAuthorization = true`. Hermit hardcodes `false` (configuration_manager.rs:160).
3. CacheSize (600 vs Jellyfin 0): Jellyfin's `CacheSize` has no initializer -> defaults to 0. Hermit hardcodes `6 * 100 = 600` (configuration_manager.rs:120) and its comment ("C# uses ProcessorCount * 100") is incorrect for this field.

INSTANCE (not bugs):
4. IsStartupWizardCompleted: harness-created Jellyfin has run the startup wizard (StartupController flips it to true), Hermit is a fresh untouched instance so it is false. Runtime state, not a default divergence.
5. IsPortAuthorized: set at runtime by the UPnP/port-mapping self-test; environment-dependent per instance.
proposed_fix:
Fix the three defaults in `default_server_configuration()` (crates/hermit-core/src/configuration_manager.rs) to match Jellyfin's ServerConfiguration.cs:

1. plugin_repositories (line 134): seed the default upstream repo:
   plugin_repositories: vec![hermit_model::updates::RepositoryInfo {
       name: Some("Jellyfin Stable".to_owned()),
       url: Some("https://repo.jellyfin.org/files/plugin/manifest.json".to_owned()),
       enabled: true,
   }],
   (RepositoryInfo is at crates/hermit-model/src/updates.rs:128 with name: Option<String>, url: Option<String>, enabled: bool.)

2. enable_legacy_authorization (line 160): change `false` -> `true`.

3. cache_size (lines 119-120): change to `cache_size: 0,` and drop the incorrect ProcessorCount comment. (Optional: raise cache_size as a candidate setting if a non-zero cache is desired, but the faithful Jellyfin default is 0.)

Leave IsStartupWizardCompleted (line 87, false) and is_port_authorized (line 94, false) as-is; both are correct fresh-instance runtime state, not port defaults.
faithfulness: Jellyfin's ServerConfiguration.cs constructor seeds exactly one PluginRepositories entry ("Jellyfin Stable" -> repo.jellyfin.org manifest, Enabled=true), defaults EnableLegacyAuthorization to true, and leaves CacheSize at its type default 0. IsStartupWizardCompleted starts false on a truly fresh install (the harness's Jellyfin only reads true because its startup wizard was completed during setup); IsPortAuthorized is set at runtime by port-mapping detection. So the three seeded-default fields are faithfulness bugs; the two boolean-state fields are faithful and merely reflect instance/setup state.
collision_risk: Low. default_server_configuration() is the single seed point; changing three literals is localized. Check for tests asserting these exact defaults (crates/hermit-model/src/configuration.rs tests mod at line 1169, and any configuration_manager tests) and update expected values there. No serde/contract shape change (fields already present and correctly typed). Existing on-disk system.json files keep their persisted values (load path reads the file verbatim), so only fresh installs pick up the corrected defaults.
verify: After editing, on a fresh data dir run the server and curl the endpoint: `cargo run -p hermit-server -- --data-dir /tmp/hcfg --port 8096` then `curl -s -H 'Authorization: MediaBrowser Token="..."' http://localhost:8096/System/Configuration | jq '{CacheSize, EnableLegacyAuthorization, PluginRepositories}'`. Expect CacheSize=0, EnableLegacyAuthorization=true, PluginRepositories=[{Name:"Jellyfin Stable", Url:"https://repo.jellyfin.org/files/plugin/manifest.json", Enabled:true}]. Then `cargo nextest run -p hermit-core -p hermit-model` to catch any default-asserting tests.

root_cause: Hermit's `get_public_users` mis-ports Jellyfin's `UserController.GetPublicUsers`. In real Jellyfin BOTH branches call `Get(isHidden:false, isDisabled:false, …)` — i.e. hidden and disabled users are ALWAYS excluded from /Users/Public. The `IsStartupWizardCompleted` flag only toggles the device+network filters (the 3rd/4th args: false,false when the wizard is incomplete, true,true once complete), NOT the hidden/disabled filter. Hermit instead gates the hidden/disabled filter itself on the wizard flag: when the wizard is complete it passes Some(false),Some(false) (correct hidden/disabled behavior), but when the wizard is INCOMPLETE it passes None,None — returning every user with no hidden/disabled filtering at all (crates/hermit-api/src/handlers/users.rs:467-471). In the differential harness Hermit's wizard is never completed: benchmark/bench-lib.js:106 runs jellyfinFirstRunWizard() only for target==='jellyfin', and Hermit's config default is is_startup_wizard_completed:false (crates/hermit-core/src/configuration_manager.rs:87), only ever flipped by POST /Startup/Complete (handlers/startup.rs:84) which the harness never calls for Hermit. So Jellyfin (wizard done) runs the hidden/disabled filter and Hermit (wizard not done) does not — any hidden or disabled user leaks from Hermit as an unmatched array element, which parity-diff.js aligns by Name and reports as an "extra (whole item)". The device/network narrowing Hermit omits is legitimately deferred (no network manager) and is a no-op for the harness's anonymous localhost request anyway, so it is not the cause.
proposed_fix: In crates/hermit-api/src/handlers/users.rs, make the hidden/disabled filter unconditional (matching Jellyfin's `Get(false, false, …)` in BOTH branches) instead of gating it on the wizard flag. Replace the wizard-conditional body of get_public_users (lines 462-472) with a single call: `let dtos = filtered_user_dtos(&state, Some(false), Some(false)).await?; Ok(Json(dtos))`. Drop the `wizard_done`/config lookup entirely. The wizard flag in Jellyfin only toggles the device (filterByDevice) and network (filterByNetwork) filters — both of which Hermit already omits by design and which are no-ops for an anonymous local-network request — so removing the wizard branch loses nothing Hermit implements while fixing the hidden/disabled semantics. Update the doc comment (lines 451-454) which currently states the inverted rule ("Before the startup wizard completes, every user is returned"): Jellyfin actually excludes hidden/disabled users in both cases.
faithfulness: Real Jellyfin: GetPublicUsers returns Get(false,false,false,false) when !IsStartupWizardCompleted else Get(false,false,true,true). Get() unconditionally excludes IsDisabled and IsHidden users (isHidden/isDisabled args are false in both calls); filterByDevice uses the request DeviceId (empty for an anonymous call → no-op) and filterByNetwork skips users lacking EnableRemoteAccess only when the caller is NOT in the local network (localhost/docker → in-network → no-op). Result is OrderBy(Username). So on any real deployment a hidden or disabled user never appears on /Users/Public regardless of wizard state.
collision_risk: Low. Single handler function in users.rs; the shared filtered_user_dtos helper already supports Some(false),Some(false) (used by the wizard-done path today) and reads is_hidden/is_disabled from UserPolicy (user_manager.rs:1068-1069), so no manager/DB change is needed. GetUsers (the authenticated sibling) has its own filter args and is untouched. No contract/route-table change.
verify: Unit/handler test: seed two users, mark one IsHidden (or IsDisabled), leave is_startup_wizard_completed=false, GET /Users/Public → assert only the non-hidden/non-enabled-off user is returned (currently returns both). Or end-to-end against the harness: on a fresh Hermit (wizard not completed) create a hidden user via POST /Users/New + policy, then curl http://localhost:8096/Users/Public and confirm the hidden user is absent — matching Jellyfin, which excludes it in both wizard states.
